mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which reduces real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous value + 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS rise < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 5,000 jobs over two consecutive months predicts stronger consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥5,000 over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the identified employment increase, or the increase is <5,000 jobs in both months.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real private demand) grows faster than CPIAUCSL (inflation) for three consecutive quarters, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive due to stronger real income growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive when the condition holds (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by at least 10% in a month is associated with supply-side weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥10% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO declines by ≥10% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS > 5%, the S&P 20-day forward return is negative due to higher discount rates applied to equity prices.
regime_hint: High FED Funds rate steady regime
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for two consecutive months, wage growth expectations weaken, causing a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
regime_hint: Low unemployment and falling wage expectations
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the UNRATE decline (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in HOUST (residential construction) by over 15% in a single month signals a housing recovery, producing a positive S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >15% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the spike occurs (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS (retail sales) below 2% of trend imply weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 2% of 12-month rolling trend for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the below-trend sales (p < 0.05).
